223147.description: Xanmeer construction was an art form perfected by the Stone-Nest tribe. As their greatest artisans grew into their own, some adopted signature accents like the ones seen here.

223148.name: Stone-Nest Gazebo
223148.description: An ancient structure from the era before the arrival of Clan Corelanya. These stones have born witness to Stone-Nest ceremonies for centuries.

223149.name: Stone-Nest Counterweight
223149.description: "As we move the stones, so the stones move the world around us." - Cord-Spinner Nakish

223150.name: Stone-Nest Pendulum
223150.description: Stone-Nest ingenuity takes many shapes, many forms, as the xanmeers themselves have shifted and changed over the centuries.

223151.name: Vitrified Soul Crystal
223151.description:
"Whispers from the Wall. 
A Writhing Torrent of Souls
Soulfire Trapped Within"

223152.name: Molag Bal Statue, Fractured Arm
223152.description: Sculpted by a Dremora artisan of unusual talents, maintained by the most faithful of the cult, destroyed by heroes in a bid to end the Harvester of Souls.

223153.name: Molag Bal Statue, Fractured Head
223153.description: Sculpted by a renowned Dremora artisan, this head is rumored to have been severed by its own creator.

223154.name: Coldharbour Soul Furnace
223154.description: "We will forbid our students from using soul gems on sentients. It will take several generations and the suppression of the Worm Cult, but if the Mages Guild can't take the long view for the good of Tamriel, who can?" - Mages Guild Memo on Soul-Trapping

223155.name: Daedric Gate, Coldharbour
223155.description: Made safe by the Mages Guild, this arcane device pulled from the depths of Coldharbour still makes a handsome addition to any home.

223156.name: Reaper, Pattern Template

223661.name: Worm King's Sarcophagus, Necropolis Replica
223661.description: "Mage from infancy, blood-selected for magicka, descended from isles of Artaeum forever! Destined was I from long before birth to exceed all mortals."—Excerpted from Worm Saga by Mannimarco

223662.name: Ashbound Hall Aspect Lock, Replica
223662.description: Though this mechanism is a replica, the working locks in Ashbound Hall required special keys called Aspects to open.

223663.name: Worm Cult Banner, Hanging Red
223663.description: "We know why we're all here, gathered under this blood-red banner. Yes, siblings in necromancy, none shall stop us from achieving our greatest successes. For the King of Worms!"—Bonelord Mukhel

223664.name: Worm Cult Tent, Cultist's
223664.description: Even Worm Cultists need shelter when out in the field! Set up this tent wherever the weather can get to you, and rest easy knowing that you probably won't wake up with wet socks. Also works well as guest accommodations.

223732.name: Target Worm Colossus
223732.description: This is a large house item. This may be attacked and, when destroyed, will regenerate. This creature is equivalent to a veteran trial boss. Its abilities include granting a resource-restoring synergy opportunity, performance buffs, and self debuffs.

1.name: Palomino Horse
1.description: Handsome, strong, and swift, the palomino is favored by couriers and sportsmen.

2.name: Sorrel Horse
2.description: A hardy, well-rounded, and dependable beast.
2.hint: Acquired from the level up advisor.

3.name: Brown Paint Horse
3.description: Favored by farmers and traders, this muscular horse is strong and patient.
3.hint: Purchased from the Stablemasters located in cities throughout Tamriel.

4.name: Bay Dun Horse
4.description: This energetic mount is well-liked by battlefield scouts.
4.hint: Purchased from the Stablemasters located in cities throughout Tamriel.

5.name: Midnight Steed
5.description: A luxurious black steed, often considered a point of pride and distinction by Tamrielic jockeys, cavalry, and couriers.
5.hint: Purchased from the Stablemasters located in cities throughout Tamriel.

6.name: Imperial Horse
6.description: Impetuous and fierce, this all-purpose Imperial steed yields only to a capable master.

7.name: Nibenay Mudcrab
7.description: A frisky little crustacean pal, at home in the water or out of it.

8.name: Razak's Opus
8.description: A loyal steam-powered Dwarven Spider, fueled by magicka from a soul gem that will last for eras.
8.hint: Acquired by completing the quest "The Mystery of Razak."

9.name: Pony Guar
9.description: A favorite household pet in Morrowind, the Pony Guar is a glutton for affection.

10.name: Crony Scrib
10.description: The caramel scrib crony is a quiet companion, devoted and easily housebroken.

11.name: Imgakin Monkey
11.description: The imgakin monkey pet is lively and cheerful, even in the grimmest of dungeons.
11.hint: Acquired by playing in The Elder Scrolls Online Beta.

12.name: Whiterun Wolfhound
12.description: The hunting dog of the Nords of Skyrim, known to face down sabre cats for their masters.

13.name: Rufous Mudcrab
13.description: A perky crab buddy whose rust-colored shell covers a cheerful, inquisitive demeanor.

14.name: Bristlegut Piglet
14.description: This cross between a domestic pig and a Skyrim boar is as loyal as it is adorable.

15.name: Frisky Scrib
15.description: This lambent little larva loves crawling alongside valorous adventurers!

16.name: High Hrothgar Wraith
16.description: An ice wraith from the slopes of the highest mountain in Tamriel.
16.hint: This unique pet is granted as a token of appreciation to players who remained subscribed to The Elder Scrolls Online for three months.

17.name: Loyal Dwarven Sphere
17.description: A Dwarven Sphere of the long-lost Dwemer.
17.hint: This unique pet is granted as a token of appreciation to players who remained subscribed to The Elder Scrolls Online for six months.

18.name: Green Narsis Guar
18.description: The robust Green Narsis is the standard mount and dray-beast of central Morrowind.

19.name: Golden Eye Guar
19.description: A crossbreed of banded and wild guar, as fearsome as it is intelligent and difficult to control.

20.name: Banded Guar Charger
20.description: A breed of guar bred for cavalry use, able to carry an armored warrior into battle.

21.name: Tessellated Guar
21.description: A sturdy, multi-purpose guar, at home anywhere from swamps to the ashlands.

22.name: Senche-Leopard
22.description: A mount bred for bearing an armed warrior while slinking through the steamy jungles of Pellitine.

23.name: Clouded Senche-Leopard
23.description: A strong yet nimble mount, bred for hunting in the Tenmar forest.

24.name: Black Senche-Panther
24.description: A mount said to have been bred by Baandari Pedlars for ease in hastily leaving town after dark.

25.name: Senche-Lioness
25.description: These fierce and powerful mounts hail from the broad savannahs of Anequina.

26.name: Banekin
26.description: Though unwilling to fight, this Daedric minion will follow you loyally—for now.

27.name: Blackwood Monkey
27.description: This busy little buddy is sometimes mistaken for an imgakin monkey.

28.name: Vermilion Scuttler
28.description: A reptilian pal from Morrowind, where they're known for quickness, devotion, and a mildly offensive odor.
28.hint: Obtained by pre-purchasing the Explorer's Pack.

29.name: Bravil Retriever
29.description: The Bravil Retriever loves the water and is a favorite hunter's companion from Anvil to Gideon.

30.name: Helstrom Ancestor Lizard
30.description: Some scholars believe Argonians are descended—or were uplifted—from these tree-dwelling swamp lizards. True or not, they make great pets, affectionate and low-maintenance.

31.name: Daedric Scamp
31.description: A foul-smelling Daedric minion, who will follow you loyally, though it won't fight for you.

32.name: Windhelm Wolfhound
32.description: Descended from royal hunting dogs, Windhelm Wolfhounds are known as steadfast companions.

33.name: Housecat
33.description: This green-eyed feline is a distant relative of the Alfiq Khajiit.

35.name: Striped Senche-Tiger
35.description: A semi-domesticated version of the wild senche-tiger, this distant relative of the Khajiit has been bred for size and manageability.
35.hint: This unique mount was granted as a token of appreciation to players who remained subscribed to The Elder Scrolls Online from April 2014 through June 2015.

37.name: Sea Sapphire Dovah-Fly
37.description: Often accompanying ships as they leave port, each blue-purple iridescent Dovah-Fly chooses a person to follow. Each night, the whirr of its gently flitting wings pull its chosen one to slumber, and at sunrise it lightly lands on its "pet" to wake them up.

41.name: Regal Dovah-Fly
41.description: Many a Vvardenfell youngster growing up in the swamps of West Gash or the Bitter Coast remembers spending happy hours playing "dodge-dovah" with these hovering bug-buddies! If hand-raised from larval form, they can become devoted companion animals.

43.name: Daedrat
43.description: This scurrying vermin from Oblivion would be lost in the vastness of Nirn without a loyal companion and guide. Even a Daedric rodent needs a friend.

55.name: White Mane Horse
55.description: A rare, highly sought cross between a midnight steed and a Skyrim ice-horse.

56.name: Dapple Gray Palfrey
56.description: Elegant and intelligent, this breed of horse is a favorite among the nobles of Cyrodiil.

57.name: Piebald Destrier
57.description: Staunch and vigorous, this patterned war-horse is known for its courage and tenacity.

58.name: Gray Yokudan Charger
58.description: These chargers are descended from the great gray war-horses of the Ra Gada.

59.name: Nightmare Courser
59.description: The origin of this horrific mount is obscure, but some see the hand of Mehrunes Dagon in it.

61.name: Bantam Guar
61.description: According to the calculations of the sages of the Cult of the Ancestor Moth, the Bantam Guar is the cutest creature in all Tamriel.

62.name: Alik'r Dune-Hound
62.description: The Dune-Hound is the loyal dog of the Redguard hunters of the Alik'r.
62.hint: Acquired from the level up advisor.

63.name: Striped Senche-Panther
63.description: This elegant senche-panther is a distant relative of the Khajiit, though it cannot speak like the cat-folk.

67.name: Amber Ash Hopper
67.description: Native to the upper Ashlands and the slopes of Red Mountain, the perky Amber Ash Hopper is a favorite pet of Dunmer expatriates, as it's relatively low maintenance (it digs its own hole in the ground), and it reminds the Dark Elves of home.

68.name: Deep-Moss Ash Hopper
68.description: The Deep-Moss Ash Hopper is native to southern Vvardenfell, where it's most commonly found in the fungal-forested uplands and the coastal marshes. They've been adopted as mascot bugs by the Buoyant Armigers, who admire their green carapaces.

69.name: Ruby Shroom Shalk
69.description: The Ruby Shroom Shalk is a popular house pet on the Telvanni Coast; the sway of its warm red fungus caps as it waddles about in the firelight of a parlor hearth just says "I'm home" to Dark Elves of a sentimental nature.

77.name: Blue-Cap Shroom Shalk
77.description: For the Dark Elves, the Shroom Shalk is a companion animal that brings calm and serenity to the Dunmeri home. There's just something so soothing about the way the blue fungal sprouts on its back gently wave and puff out spores as the beast putters about.

78.name: Bitter Coast Cliff Strider
78.description: Thetys Ramarys of Balmora says, "I love our Bitter Coast Striders, but feel bad that they can't fly very well. So I'm selectively breeding them into a strain that, one day, will dominate the Vvardenfell skies, pursuing its prey for great distances!"

86.name: Shornhelm Shepherd
86.description: This hardy dog was bred for herding sheep in the rugged terrain of Rivenspire.

88.name: Freckled Guar
88.description: Known in Deshaan as loyal pals, the Freckled is the most intelligent breed of guar.

89.name: Gold-Cap Shroom Shalk
89.description: It isn't well known outside financial circles, but somewhere in the basement or sub-level of every bank in Morrowind you'll find the institution's mascot, a sweet old waddling Gold-Cap Shroom Shalk. The symbolism, of course, is obvious.

90.name: Boralis Gray Wolf Pup
90.description: When the gray wolves of Rivenspire howl across the dismal moors of Boralis, it sends a chill down the spine and even the bravest look back over their shoulders—but by Kynareth, their pups sure are cute! And adorably playful into the bargain.

91.name: Striated Pony Guar
91.description: A favorite household pet in Morrowind, the Striated Pony Guar is a glutton for affection.

92.name: White River Ice Wolf Pup
92.description: The Ice Wolves that lope along the White River of northeast Skyrim are associated with both the goddess Mara and the Wolf Totem of Atmora—but it's mighty hard to think of their mythic stature when you're rolling around in the snow with an Ice Wolf Puppy!

93.name: Frost Mare
93.description: With its icy gaze and steaming breath, the frigid Frost Mare seems carved from the very glaciers of Skyrim.

102.name: Doom Wolf Pup
102.description: When a Doom Wolf Pup looks at you with its big red eyes, you may just melt inside—but as soon as you turn your back, that little rascal will be shredding your embroidered Arenthian pillows and digging up your herbal garden.

103.name: Solitude Silver Wolf
103.description: Common sights around Solitude, these steadfast and fierce wolves also adorn the heraldry of that city. All of them are, of course, good wolves, and befriending one brings you good fortune in the land of the Nords!
103.hint: Acquired by completing the "The Vampire Scholar" quest in Western Skyrim.

104.name: Skeletal Pony Guar
104.description: Shouldn't an animated skeleton always be a thing of fear and revulsion? This necromantic Pony Guar might change your mind about that!

111.name: Fennec Fox
111.description: A native of Hammerfell, the Fennec Fox has been domesticated by many of its desert peoples, and makes an alert and loyal pet.

112.name: Purple Daggerback
112.description: The glowing Purple Daggerback boar is found only in Craglorn in the vicinity of the Spellscar, from which it seems to have absorbed some sort of magical aura.

113.name: Mind-Shriven Horse
113.description: With its equine psyche stolen by Daedric magic, the mind-shriven horse is a docile yet terrifying mount.

114.name: Red Pit Wolf Pup
114.description: The Red Pit Wolves of southern Skyrim are known for their aggression and ferocity, and you can see that even in their puppies, adorable as they are. They love to play, but that means play-fighting, so expect to get chewed on as you tussle!

133.name: Abecean Ratter Cat
133.description: The Abecean Ratter is famed from Hegathe to Woodhearth as a prime rodent-catcher.
133.hint: Acquired from the level up advisor.

134.name: Senchal Striped Cat
134.description: The Senchal Striped is a cat that is as cunning as it is elegant. It's both cursed at and admired for its ability to get into places it doesn't belong.

135.name: Necrom Ghostgazer Cat
135.description: The Necrom Ghostgazer is the favored feline companion of Telvanni wizards. They not only keep the skeevers down, but they can "see" intruding demons and spirits.

136.name: Markarth Bear-Dog
136.description: Fierce and courageous fighters, the hunters of Western Skyrim use small packs of these dogs to pursue bears. The Bear-Dogs track, corner, and harry the bears until the hunters can arrive with their spears.

143.name: Baby Netch
143.description: Once this young Netch calf imprints on a master, it will follow him or her anywhere, floating along and tootling happily.

144.name: Ninendava Sacred Goat
144.description: The goats that come from the ruin of Ninendava in Cyrodiil are no mere domestic livestock. They have long been used in certain forbidden Daedric rituals—and have even been known to lead mortals through those arcane rites.

145.name: Bal Foyen Nix-Hound
145.description: Who says a giant, aggressive, blood-sucking insect can't make a loveable pet? Not the Dark Elves of Bal Foyen, who breed them as trackers, watch-hounds, and netch-deflators.

149.name: Stonefire Scamp
149.description: This gibbering, foul-smelling Daedric minion will follow you loyally, though it won't fight for you.
149.hint:
A rare reward from defeating the elite Daedric forces and their master in the Darkest Depths.

Can also be acquired from the Impresario during Guilds and Glory.

150.name: Imperial War Mastiff
150.description: Mastiffs are the most common breed used by the Imperial Legions as battle dogs. The Imperial War Mastiff in particular is the mascot and symbol of the storied Second Legion, headquartered in peacetime in the vicinity of Bruma.

151.name: Cave Bear
151.description: Found throughout Tamriel's northern mountains, the Cave Bear makes a hardy and imposing mount.

153.name: Copperback Bear-Dog
153.description: The Copperback variant of the Markarth Bear-Dog is renowned for its responsiveness to training, but keep an eye on it, or will get into all sorts of mischief. Especially keep an eye on its eyes, which are two different colors!

155.name: Fiendroth
155.description: Who doesn't want to be followed around by a hulking, armored Daedric bug with steel mandibles and a venomous stinger? It eats nothing but the cries and lamentations of your enemies, so it's an easy keeper. Friendly, too—in its way.

156.name: Pocket Mammoth
156.description: Pocket Mammoths were originally bred small in order to make them more manageable as livestock, but in Wrothgar some escaped and began breeding in the wild. However, they're easily domesticated, especially if you get one when it's young.

157.name: Dragontail Goat
157.description: The brown Goats of the Dragontail Mountains are stronger than they look. There's a saying in Hammerfell: "Hits as hard as a Dragontail ram!"

158.name: Sanguine's Black Goat
158.description: A goat bred to take part in Daedric rituals? Nonsense. It's just a goat. Isn't it? But why does it look at you like that? And did it just … whisper? No. It's just a goat!

159.name: Chub Loon
159.description: A denizen of Tamriel's northern shores, the Chub Loon survives on the bounty of the sea, dining on small fish of all types. Though clumsy and awkward on shore, it flies gracefully and is a nimble swimmer. Best of all, they make affectionate pets.

160.name: Echalette
160.description: Full-grown echateres may be stubborn and ornery, but the baby Echalettes are playful and, frankly, just plain adorable. Once a young Echalette bonds with its master, it becomes a devoted companion.
160.hint: Acquired by traveling to Orsinium for the first time.

163.name: Necrotic Hoarvor
163.description: Your new best friend is a giant blood-sucking insect bloated with pustulant, lethal contagion! It's bursting with both infection and affection—for you!
163.hint: Acquired by completing the "Imperial City Challenger" achievement in the Imperial City.

164.name: Skeletal Horse
164.description: Behold the Skeletal Horse! Mortal races are not the only creatures that can be re-animated by necromancers. The best part: no need to muck out the stable.

165.name: Skeletal Senche
165.description: The Skeletal Senche may be the most fearsome of all feline mounts. Expertly re-animated, even in undead form it retains all the lithe strength it possessed in life.

166.name: Skeletal Guar
166.description: The naked, grisly smile on the broad skull of the Skeletal Guar mount may be enough to send lesser opponents fleeing in terror when you ride into battle on its creaking, bony frame. The Worm Cult, of course, will just be jealous.

173.name: Zombie Horse
173.description: Mannimarco's Order of the Black Worm must be responsible for the re-animated Zombie Horse, as it was first seen in Cyrodiil as a Worm Anchorite's mount.

177.name: Snow Bear
177.description: The Snow Bear makes a superior mount for northern climes, as it's undaunted by even the fiercest winter weather.

178.name: Black Bear
178.description: The Black Bear is common across Cyrodiil, but is also seen north into High Rock and Skyrim, where it is considered a warrior's mount.

189.name: Skeletal Bear
189.description: A re-animated Skeletal Bear makes a fearsome mount, and is a favorite of northern Tamriel's necromancers.

190.name: Black Bear Cub
190.description: The Black Bear Cub is both playful and affectionate, and is so adorable it's quickly forgiven for whatever trouble it gets into.

191.name: Cave Bear Cub
191.description: The Cave Bear Cub may miss its mountain home, but that just makes it twice as loyal to its mortal companion.

192.name: Psijic Domino Pig
192.description: Originally bred on the Isle of Artaeum, the black-and-white Domino Pig is so smart it can count to five and learn to recognize its name.

193.name: Snow Bear Cub
193.description: The Snow Bear is known for its fierceness, but its cub is as cute as a bug. Maybe even two bugs.

221.name: Black Mask Bear-Dog
221.description: This variant of the Bear-Dog is a favorite of the Markarth Watch—and of the thieves who attempt to evade them. The Watch uses them to sniff out trouble, while the outlaws employ them to keep an eye out for the Watch!

222.name: Mossy Netch Calf
222.description: The greenish, or "Mossy" Netches, are most commonly found in the West Gash region of northwest Vvardenfell. The calves are docile, even for Netches, and will happily follow along behind anyone who smells of their favorite fungi.

231.name: Pale Velothi Guar
231.description: This stalwart mount comes from the ashlands downwind of the volcanoes of the Velothi Mountains, and is well adapted to surviving under the harshest of conditions.

232.name: Moonlight Senche-Tiger
232.description: The Moonlight Senche-Tigers have been the sleek and silvery guardians of the Khajiiti temples of the moons ever since the revelation of the Riddle'Thar.

233.name: Hammerfell Camel
233.description: This is the stoic, hard-working beast that riders in the wastes of Hammerfell count on to survive. And if things come to a fight, it's just plain mean.

234.name: Zeht's Cloud Camel
234.description: The white camel is said to be sacred to Zeht, the Redguard god of food and farming. The devout folk of Hammerfell bow when a Cloud Camel rides past.

235.name: Black Camel of Ill Omen
235.description: Most riders consider Black Camels to be creatures of bad luck and misfortune. But if you're a thief riding off into the night with your ill-gotten gains, you might see things differently.

242.name: Kindlespit Dragon Frog
242.description: The common or Kindlespit Dragon Frog is an engagingly preposterous little pal whose antics never fail to amuse. Hammerfell tales say the huge Dragons of ancient legend were all turned into these tiny flame-puffing hoppers.

243.name: Tangerine Dragon Frog
243.description: The slug-like Sloads of Thras bred the flame-hued Tangerine Dragon Frog so they could be spotted more easily in their archipelago's murky lagoons. Some say they were bred to be pets, but the Sload word for them translates as "snacks."

244.name: Blue Oasis Dragon Frog
244.description: The comical Blue Oasis Dragon Frog is native to Hew's Bane, and before they were bred as pets could be found only on that Hammerfell peninsula. These little bug-eaters are popular mascots at open-air taverns.

253.name: Rosy Netch Calf
253.description: The reddish, or "Rosy" Netches are native to the foyadas of the Molag Amur region of Vvardenfell, where they live in a semi-wild state subject to the occasional round-ups of the Netchimen. The calves, sulfurous odor aside, are quite adorable.

260.name: Senche-Lion Cub
260.description: If you domesticate a Senche-Lion Cub when it's young enough, it will follow you everywhere, no matter how dangerous. And your enemies will burn from the cuteness.

261.name: Dro-m'Athra Senche
261.description: The Senche-shaped dro-m'Athra are known to the Twilight Cantors as the sar-m'Athra, but everyone else just calls these eerie and uncanny mounts the Dro-m'Athra Senche.

262.name: Masked Bear
262.description: Both swift and strong, the Masked Bear of the Jerall Mountains is a popular mount along the high passes between Bruma and Falkreath.

263.name: Sabre Cat
263.description:
The sabre cats of northern Tamriel are possibly even more powerful than their southern Senche cousins. They are certainly more feral and difficult to train. 
|cFFFFFF
Riding Skill does not affect this mount's appearance.|r

265.name: Pride-King Lion
265.description: The Pride-King Lions are the top predators on the savannahs of Northern Elsweyr. No one but the Khajiit, with their feline intuitions, could have persuaded these proud beasts to serve as mounts.

266.name: Skeletal Camel
266.description: The Redguard hatred of necromancy means undead creatures are rare in Hammerfell—which will make you all the more special when you clatter into the oasis on the back of a terrifying Skeletal Camel!

267.name: Tythis Andromo, the Banker
267.description:
This aristocratic banker is on hand whenever he's needed, available for all personal banking services—except in Cyrodiil or Battlegrounds, which are far too dangerous for this fellow.

When summoned, his services can be used by you and your groupmates.

268.name: Sylvan Nixad
268.description: Once a common sight in Cyrodiil's Great Forest, the Sylvan Nixad is now most often encountered in the glades and meadows of the Gold Coast. Once tamed, they make charming companions, loyal and easy to care for.

269.name: Turquoise Nixad
269.description: Scholars think the iridescent blue Turquoise Nixad must have inherent magical properties, because those wings certainly aren't big enough to enable it to fly. Yet fly it does, flitting about like a beautiful human-shaped hummingbird moth.

270.name: Orchid Nixad
270.description: The rarest of these fay creatures is the Orchid Nixad, said to be sacred to the goddess Dibella, and found only in wild places hallowed to her worship. It's known that the Empress Tavia had an Orchid Nixad as a friend and companion.

290.name: Highland Wolf
290.description: The brown Highland Wolf is common in the Colovian hills and in Cyrodiil's Great Forest, where wild packs are feared by farmers and shepherds. But foresters have domesticated the beasts and, bred for size, use them as mounts.

291.name: Doom Wolf
291.description: Bred for size and savagery from the fierce timber wolves of the southern Jerall Mountains, the Doom Wolf has been adopted as the mount of choice by the secretive and deadly Dark Brotherhood.

292.name: Ice Wolf
292.description: The Ice Wolf of the far north can grow to tremendous size—which is probably why the Nords of Hjaalmarch decided to ride them. Domesticating giant Ice Wolves wasn't an easy task, but it's just the kind of challenge a Nord loves.

293.name: Wild Hunt Horse
293.description: When the Wood Elves invoke the Wild Hunt, creatures forget their Y'ffre-taught shapes and shift into unnatural forms. Such are the Wild Hunt Horses, mounts that occupy a space between flora and fauna.

294.name: Wild Hunt Guar
294.description: Wild Hunt Guar are mounts that have reverted to the shapeshifting chaos of the Dawn Era. They have become part plant and part animal, as wonderful as they are abominable.

295.name: Wild Hunt Senche
295.description: The Wild Hunt unravels the shapes Y'ffre established for creatures in the Dawn Era, transforming them into monstrous but vigorous hybrid beasts. Among these, both beautiful and abhorrent, is the Wild Hunt Senche-Mount.

296.name: Wild Hunt Bear
296.description: The Wild Hunt Bear is a forest beast that has lost its Y'ffre-given ability to choose between being plant or animal, reverting to the primal chaos of the Dawn Era.

297.name: Wild Hunt Camel
297.description: Y'ffre's Naming gave all the creatures of Nirn their shapes, even in the arid deserts of Tamriel. When its name comes magically unraveled, then a creature begins to forget its shape and devolve to a state between flora and fauna. Thus the Wild Hunt Camel.

298.name: Wild Hunt Wolf
298.description: Some say that Hircine meddled with the nature of wolves in a way that made them susceptible to shape-shifting, and from this Daedric interference came both the Werewolf—and the Wild Hunt Wolf. What is the truth of this? Y'ffre knows!

299.name: Skeletal Wolf
299.description: It's said that when King Styriche, the Vampire of Verkarth, led his Gray Host west to Bangkorai, his terrible Zombie Hussars were mounted on a great pack of Skeletal Wolves. Some escaped the massacre of the Gray Host, and survived to haunt the wastes.

300.name: Pirharri the Smuggler
300.description:
This Baandari Pedlar is on hand whenever she's needed (except in Cyrodiil and Battlegrounds), and will fence any of your goods for you—but she'll take a cut of the profits.

When summoned, her services can only be used by you.
300.hint: Acquired by completing the Thieves Guild questline.

301.name: Nuzhimeh the Merchant
301.description:
This alert merchant is on hand whenever she's needed, and will buy any non-stolen goods you or your group offer her. She won't come to Cyrodiil or Battlegrounds, though—too dangerous.

When summoned, her services can be used by you and your groupmates.

303.name: Sabre Leopard Cub
303.description: "For the Mages Guild, I devised an enchanted 'appealometer' that measures creatures' adorableness," says Researcher Neotenus. "After tests on other pets, I tried to take a reading on a Sabre Snow Leopard Cub, but the device overloaded and shattered."

304.name: Alliance War Dog
304.description:
War Dogs can be found in the armies of all three Alliances, mainly in the capacity of aides to the military police. They are as loyal to their masters as they are savage to their enemies.

|cFFFFFF(Appearance is specific to your character's alliance.)

305.name: Black Mane Lion
305.description: At the Palace of the Mane near Torval, by tradition the Bi-Lunar Guard are all mounted on matching Black Mane Lions, which are reserved for them alone. So be wary if you ride your Black Mane near Torval, lest you anger the Bi-Lunars!

313.name: White Lion
313.description: In Elsweyr, the White Lion is considered a highly prestigious mount. When King Keirgo married Queen Eshita, his Orcrest Honor Guard, twenty strong, were all mounted on mature White Lions.

314.name: Hearthfire Kagouti
314.description: The Hearthfire Kagouti appears to be a sort of magical hybrid, a wizard's experimental melding of a carnivorous reptile and a flame atronach. The fact that they were first sighted in the Telvanni Grazelands lends this theory some credence.

324.name: Northern Lynx
324.description: Native to Tamriel's northern forests, in the wild the Lynx lives on a diet of rabbits, hares, and skeevers. Domesticated, the Lynx makes a dignified and stylish animal companion, popular with the Nord aristocracy.

325.name: Colovian Badger
325.description: Though Badgers mainly eat burrowing rodents, farmers hate them because they'll take chickens, kwama scribs, and bantam guar if they get the chance. Cranky and irritable, they make terrible pets—which makes them a favorite among the Undaunted.

326.name: Red Pit Wolf
326.description: Pit Wolves are so called because they were bred by the Reachmen as fierce pit fighters, often matched against bears or bristlebacks. In order to make his guards more impressive, the Tyrant of Markarth was the first to have Red Pits trained as mounts.

355.name: Dominion Lizard-Locks
355.description: Going to war may mean donning a helm, but beneath it an Argonian Dominion warrior is entitled to wear these official Alliance Lizard-Locks, which keep beaded bristles under control while still looking superb.

357.name: Snowy Sabre Cat Cub
357.description: This little cub loves to play in the snow, but don't let it get lost in the deep drifts—and when you pull it out, be careful of those little sabre teeth!

360.name: Jackal
360.description: The Jackal of Tamriel is called by some the "thieves' dog" because it's quick to sniff out sources of food, and clever enough to figure out how to get at them. Once tamed, they serve as loyal companions.
360.hint: Acquired by traveling to Abah's Landing for the first time.

364.name: Clockwork Shalk
364.description: The Clockwork Shalk is a fabricant from the hidden laboratories of Sotha Sil. It seems programmed to obey the master it imprints upon, but who knows what secret orders it will follow if events occur to trigger them?

365.name: Alliance War Horse
365.description:
It's no surprise the Three Alliances compete to breed the strongest and most majestic chargers for their armored cavalries.
|cFFFFFF
Appearance is linked to your character's alliance.

Riding Skill does not affect this mount's appearance.|r

391.name: Sep Adder
391.description: These flying vipers have short tempers and nasty dispositions, but just look at those cute crimson eyes! Some of them can even be trained not to inject poison when they bite. The perfect pet!

392.name: Heartland Brindle Badger
392.description: Native to the Cyrodilic Heartland, the Brindle Badger is said to be as fierce as a wolverine, yet as cunning as a fox. A Brindle Badger adorned the banners of King Hrol when he led his knights on the Quest of Sancre Tor.

393.name: M'aiq the Badger
393.description: How did this one become a so-handsome copperback Badger? M'aiq will tell you. One day near Balmora he met two Telvanni wizards, one of whom said, "Everything I tell you is true," while the other said, "Everything I tell you is a lie…."

394.name: Black Cat
394.description: This black cat knows things you cannot know, and sees things you cannot see. But that is the nature of all black cats, is it not?

395.name: Kagouti
395.description: Domesticating the savage Kagouti to serve as a mount is a recent endeavor, and to be frank, more than a little experimental. Do you have what it takes to stay in the saddle on one of these fierce, bipedal reptiles?

396.name: Allaria Erwen the Exporter
396.description:
This free-spirited merchant is happy to join your adventures and take excess loot off your hands; however, Cyrodiil and Battlegrounds are too bloody for her liking.

When summoned, she will purchase any non-stolen goods you or your groupmates offer her.

397.name: Cassus Andronicus the Mercenary
397.description:
This severe mercenary is duty bound to guard your possessions with his life. Unless you're in Cyrodiil or the Battlegrounds—his contract explicitly excludes travel there.

When summoned, his banking services are available to you and your groupmates.

400.name: Storm Atronach Horse
400.description: Summoned from the plane of Levinace, the Storm Atronach Horse is a Daedric mount of majesty and terror, ready to appear in Tamriel whenever called to your service.

402.name: Storm Atronach Guar
402.description: By modifying Koron's Peremptory Summons, the standard spell used to call atronachs from Oblivion, the conjurer can compel a Daedra to assume the form of a common Tamrielic mount—even a Guar, if so desired!

403.name: Storm Atronach Senche
403.description: It is said the great conjurer Corvus Direnni was the first to compel a Storm Atronach to assume the form of a great cat, and shocked all Balfiera Island by riding around its shores on a crackling Storm Atronach Senche!

404.name: Storm Atronach Camel
404.description: The Altmer wizard Corvus Direnni astounded High King Ar-Azal of Hammerfell by conjuring a Storm Atronach that assumed the form of a horse—but when Ar-Azal tried to stump him by commanding he summon a Storm Atronach Camel, Corvus Direnni instantly did so!

405.name: Storm Atronach Bear
405.description: According to Nord legend, in his wars against the Snow Elves the mighty Ysgramor the Harbinger rode a Storm Atronach Bear Mount conjured for him by his personal Clever Man.

406.name: Clouded Senche-Leopard Cub
406.description: Of all the varieties of wild senche-cats, the Clouded Leopard may be the most beautiful. Their cubs love to play-fight, and stalk tiny bugs with the most hilariously serious expressions.

431.name: Lizard Rhinoceros
431.description: Even more legendary than the unicorn is that imaginary two-horned beast called the rhinoceros. Live the legend with Lizard Rhinoceros horns!

443.name: Hist Guar
443.description: In Black Marsh this mount is called Scales-Seem-Daubed-with-Hist-Sap, but the rest of Tamriel just calls it the Hist Guar. It is the only subspecies of guar known to enjoy music.

468.name: Wrapped Horsetail
468.description: Gather your flowing mane into a single towering topknot with the Wrapped Horsetail, a favorite among officers and bandit leaders.

476.name: Haj Mota Hatchling
476.description: Though it may some day grow into a horrific face-eating behemoth, when it's young the Haj Mota Hatchling is undeniably cute. For a while, they are trainable, come when called, and happily waddle after their masters wherever they may go.

477.name: Desert Lynx
477.description: The Desert Lynx, or caracal lynx, is native to south central Tamriel, roaming the savannahs from Corinthe in Elsweyr as far north as West Weald in Cyrodiil. It's the totem animal of the pastoral Khajiiti tribes, and assists with managing the herds.

478.name: Infernal Sep Adder
478.description: Though it may look like it just crawled from the depths of the Deadlands, the Infernal Sep Adder is actually native to the higher altitudes of Hammerfell. As pets, they are … not affectionate. Great conversation starters, though.

483.name: Dark Moons Lynx
483.description: The Khajiit of Corinthe believe the all-black Dark Moons Lynx is the worldly incarnation of Southpaw, the feline companion to Rajhin the Footpad, god of thieves. It's said Southpaw keeps watch while Rajhin is breaking and entering.

484.name: Dwarven War Dog
484.description: This loyal beast has been trained for warfare, and will stick with you through every kind of conflict. As a bonus, it comes outfitted in ancient Dwarven dog armor, canine barding as durable today as it was when it was first made many centuries in the past.

591.name: Great Elk
591.description:
Though the Reachmen of Markarth say they were the first to successfully domesticate the Great Elk of Skyrim and break them as mounts, the Nords of Haafingar say it was really all their idea.
|cFFFFFF
Riding Skill does not affect this mount's appearance.|r

592.name: Dozen-Banded Vvardvark
592.description: This creature, unusually cute for a denizen of Vvardenfell, is a newcomer to the island whose home and origin are unknown—unless the rumors are true that it's a hybrid born from the magical laboratories of the Telvanni.

607.name: Cobalt Sep Adder
607.description: The blue-scaled Cobalt Sep Adder is the rarest of the wild varieties, and almost never seen in captivity. They are particularly prized by the royalty of Hammerfell's contentious city-states, as they're said to be able to detect poison in drinks and food.

608.name: Storm Atronach Wolf
608.description: The Storm Atronach Wolf was the favored mount of the notorious Hjeimar the Heinous, a wizard who lived in a remote tower north of Bruma, who rode his when leading his Goblin Fiends in raids on the nearby valleys.

609.name: Black Senche-Lion
609.description: The legendary preferred mount of Elsweyr's greatest thieves, the most famous Black Senche-Lion of all was Rajhin's mount Umbrage, which could both talk and, for brief periods, fly!

618.name: Pact Lizard Battle Crest
618.description: Going to war may mean donning a helm, but beneath it an Argonian Pact warrior is entitled to wear this official Alliance Battle Crest, which keeps spines under control while still looking superb.

739.name: Imperial War Horse
739.description:
When the Empire of Cyrodiil was at its height, the Imperial Legion Cavalry rode these chalk-white chargers into battle beneath the red diamond banner. 
|cFFFFFF
Riding Skill does not affect this mount's appearance.|r

740.name: Arctic Fennec Fox
740.description: The Arctic Fennec is native to the snowy shores of Skyrim's Sea of Ghosts, and the local Nords, when they spot one romping in the drifts, respond with the traditional oath of "Shor's Ears!"

741.name: Dusky Fennec Fox
741.description: The Dusky or Midnight Fennec Fox is native to the high savannah of Northern Elsweyr, and is often domesticated by nomadic tribes of Khajiit.

742.name: Tuxedo Bear
742.description: Though the famed bard Svaknir wrote a hilarious song in which the Tuxedo was mocked as "the Chub Loon of Bears," this magnificent ursine mount has been esteemed by Nord nobles since the early First Era.

743.name: Senche-Tiger Cub
743.description: It's a striped Senche-Tiger Cub. What more could you need to know? "Ah," you ask, "but is it magical?" Just look in those eyes for your answer.

745.name: Black Senche-Panther Kitten
745.description: "Rajhin the Purring Liar had so many shadows that some of them took on lives of their own, becoming black senche-panthers who stalk freely through Elsweyr—just like this kitten that plays with my tail." —Clan Mother Ahnissi

746.name: Dro-m'Athra Senche Cub
746.description: Combine Adorable with Abominable, and what do you get? The dro-m'Athra Senche Cub, the cutest thing ever to come out of the Dark Behind the World. Dance, kitten, dance!

749.name: Senche-Leopard Cub
749.description: The senche-leopard is one of the most feared predators of the Tenmar Forest in central Elsweyr, but if one of its adorable cubs can be adopted when young, it makes a fiercely loyal companion.

750.name: Striped Senche-Panther Cub
750.description: Striped senche-panthers are popular mascots of the Baandari Pedlars of Elsweyr. Incredibly adorable as cubs, even when small they can be trained like magpies to fetch shiny things back to their masters.

752.name: Ascadian Cliff Strider
752.description: This bluish breed of Vvardenfell aerial reptile, known as the Azure or Ascadian Cliff Strider, is prized by flying-lizard fanciers as the prettiest and most ornamental of its species. Bonus: its screech terrifies crying babies into silence.

761.name: Craglorn Welwa
761.description: Credit for the irresponsible and foolhardy project of domesticating the Craglorn Welwa is usually claimed by the Iron Orcs, who are always looking for ways to prove that they're "more bad-tusk" than the Orcs of Wrothgar or Skyrim.

762.name: Great Dark Stag
762.description:
The Great Dark Stag is one of the five Aspects of Hircine, invoked as Uricanbeg, "whose hooves drum the Blood Summons."
|cFFFFFF
Riding Skill does not affect this mount's appearance.|r

763.name: Nightfall Sabre Cat
763.description:
The Reachmen of the upper Karth valley, who train them as mounts, swear that the Nightfall variant is sacred to the Daedric Prince Nocturnal.
|cFFFFFF
Riding Skill does not affect this mount's appearance.|r

764.name: Sabre Cat Cub
764.description: Sabre Cats are mighty and majestic hunters that rule the northern plains and tundra by sheer strength and savagery—but, Daedra take it, they sure are cute when they're cubs!

765.name: Nightfall Sabre Cat Cub
765.description: "In my first months as a captive of the Reachmen, the only thing that made life bearable was my beloved pet, the Nightfall Sabre Cat Cub I was allowed as a companion." —Arthenice Belloq

766.name: Black Morthal Mastiff
766.description: Bull Mastiffs from Morthal in Skyrim are fearless and tireless hunters inured to the hardships of the frozen marshes. The black ones are particularly popular with mages and alchemists.

767.name: Tan Morthal Mastiff
767.description: Bull Mastiffs from Morthal in Skyrim are fearless and tireless hunters inured to the hardships of the frozen marshes. The tan variety is a favorite with scouts, hunters, and trackers.

768.name: Gray Morthal Mastiff
768.description: Bull Mastiffs from Morthal in Skyrim are fearless and tireless hunters inured to the hardships of the frozen marshes. The gray breed are quite popular with rogues, thieves, and (incongruously) priests.

769.name: Hearthfire Hatchling
769.description: Hearthfire Hatchlings, which are found only in an orphaned state, appear to be the offspring of a normal kagouti and one of the Hearthfire variety. Driven away by ordinary kagouti, these hatchlings are in grave need of adoption.

785.name: Ancestor Moth Swarm
785.description: "The Ancestor Moths that accompany some mystically-attuned mortals are more than mere insects—they are animated by the loving spirits of the dearly departed, and may grant wisdom and awareness to those they visit." —Sister Terran Arminus

786.name: Devoted Torchbug
786.description: The Wood Elves say that to be followed by a friendly Torchbug is an infallible sign of good fortune. Of course, they also catch them, dry them out, and smoke them in pipes.

812.description: One of the standard body markings available at every Tamrielic salon.

1144.name: Molag Amur Cliff Strider
1144.description: The Molag Amur Cliff Strider is prized by reptilian connoisseurs because its coloration, though somber, is lightened by its subtle golden tones. And if startled, its squawk will cause passersby to jump and horses to bolt.

1145.name: Dwarven War Horse
1145.description:
This loyal horse has been trained for warfare, and will stick with you through every kind of conflict. As a bonus, it comes outfitted in ancient Dwarven horse armor.
|cFFFFFF
Riding Skill does not affect this mount's appearance.|r

1147.name: Milady's Cloud Cat
1147.description: White cats are sacred to Dibella, the Lady of Love, and all white cats are said to be her representatives in the animal kingdom. A House of Dibella will typically have three or four milk-white cats within its walls.

1148.name: Shadowghost Senche-Panther
1148.description: In Elsweyr, being seen in the company of an uncanny Shadowghost Senche-Panther will put one under suspicion of being a Namiira cultist—or even a disguised dro-m'Athra.

1152.name: Snowy Sabre Cat
1152.description:
Of all Tamriel's great felines, the Snowy Sabre Cat is the hardiest when it comes to winter weather, barely noticing the Atmoran gales as they come howling in across the Sea of Ghosts. 
|cFFFFFF
Riding Skill does not affect this mount's appearance.|r

1155.name: Dwarven Spider
1155.description: A loyal Dwarven Spider liberated from a Dwemer ruin, converted, using the "Neramo Method," to an unlocked and autonomous state that enables it to leave its original locale.

1157.name: Snow Leopard Sabre Cat
1157.description:
The shamans of the Skaal tribe domesticated the Snow Leopard Sabres as mounts, but to keep them exclusive their breeding was restricted, and they are down to a dwindling few.
|cFFFFFF
Riding Skill does not affect this mount's appearance.|r

1159.name: Dwarven Horse
1159.description: The ancient Deep Elves made animunculi of many kinds, imitating nature with mechanical constructs. The Dwarven word for mount was "vamidium," but their equine automata are more commonly known as Dwarven Horses.

1160.name: Dwarven Senche
1160.description: Since nearly all Dwemer sites are in northeast Tamriel, where the only large feline is the sabre cat, scholars of Dwarven civilization have long wondered why they chose to make animunculi mounts that resemble the senche-tigers of the south. It's a mystery!

1161.name: Dwarven Bear
1161.description: Scholar of the Dwemer Guylaine Marilie theorized that bear vamidiums were animunculi mounts reserved only for those Deep Elves of high rank or status. "Imagine a noble in full armor on a Dwarven Bear Mount," he wrote. "What could be more impressive?"

1162.name: Dwarven Guar
1162.description: Guar vamidiums, or Dwarven Guar Mounts, are most often associated with Dwemer sites in Morrowind—as might be expected, since that's where guar are most in use as pack and riding animals.

1163.name: Dwarven Camel
1163.description: Dwarven Camels are most often found among the ruins of the desert-dwelling Rourken clan of the Dwemer, who left northeast Tamriel and traveled west to found cities in the remote back-country of Hammerfell.

1164.name: Dwarven Wolf
1164.description: Dwarven Wolves, or Lupine Vamidiums, are most often seen in proximity to Dwemer ruins of northern and western Skyrim, where wolves are most common in the wild. Its loping gait is said to give the most comfortable ride of any mechanical mount.

1170.name: Seht's Dovah-Fly
1170.description: These are clearly fabricants, clockwork simulations of living creatures, with the distinctive appearance of the handiwork of Sotha Sil. But if so, how did they escape Clockwork City? What powers them? And why do they make such loyal pets? No one knows.

1171.name: Vvardenfell Scale Model
1171.description: Librarian Bradyn presented you with this scale model of the island of Vvardenfell—a miniature version of the replica in the library in Vivec City.
1171.hint: Acquired by finding all of the ancestral tombs of Vvardenfell and the lost Library of Andule.

1173.name: Brassilisk
1173.description: "The Brassilisk is created from interconnected brass squares, its exposed copper wiring allowing for its snakelike movement. Popular as a pet, you'll often see them following the quick footsteps of young scholars." —Endilaril, Clockwork City Naturalist

1174.name: Ebon Dwarven Wolf
1174.description: "There is no evidence that the Dwemer kept dogs, or pets of any other kind, for that matter, but like their neighbors the Nords they did seem to have some affection for the Wolves of northern Tamriel. One sees this in their mounts." —Thelwe Ghelein
1174.hint: Acquired by digging up its various parts via the Antiquities system.

1184.name: Gorne Striped Wolf
1184.description: The Isle of Gorne off the east coast of Morrowind is home to many strange creatures found nowhere else in Tamriel. One of these is the giant Striped Wolf, packs of which terrorized the island's settlers till they were suppressed in the Troubled House Hunt.

1185.name: Dwarven Spider
1185.description: Of all the Dwemer animunculi, the Dwarven Spider is perhaps the most familiar and iconic. This versatile construct comes in several variations, and it should come as no surprise that one of them is a vamidium, or mechanical mount. Clankin'!

1186.name: Chroma-Blue Dwarven Spider
1186.description: Rarest of all Dwarven Spider vamidiums are those powered by gems that emit a cold blue light, said to reflect the frigid stolen soul of the Dwemer engineer trapped within it.

1187.name: Kagouti Fabricant
1187.description: Wheeled constructs and fabricants do just fine in most regions of the Clockwork City, but for traversing rough synthetic terrain, Seht's Apostles prefer the tough and capable Kagouti Fabricant mount.

1188.name: Pellitine Mustang
1188.description: The small equines of the subtropical Pellitine forests have subtle vertical stripes for camouflage under the canopy. They've been crossed with the larger Anequine Mustang to create a striking striped mount, the favorite of the First Corinthe Hussars.

1189.name: Adamant Dwarven Horse
1189.description: Though Dwemer constructs are made mostly of so-called Dwarven Metal, some rare animunculi have parts forged from a super-hard whitish alloy known to blacksmiths as Dwarven Adamant. It's one of the rarest materials on Nirn.

1190.name: Adamant Dwarven Senche
1190.description: There have long been unconfirmed reports of Dwarven Senche vamidiums with key parts made of the extremely rare and super-hard Dwarven Adamant metal. At long last, these reports have been substantiated.

1191.name: Adamant Dwarven Wolf
1191.description: The shining metal known as Dwarven Adamant is an alloy melding ores of unknown origin into the most durable material ever made. Though found in parts of the ultra-rare Adamant Dwarven Wolf, the secret of its forging seems as lost as the Dwemer themselves.

1194.name: Tuxedo Vvardvark
1194.description: The most popular conjecture about the origin of the Vvardvark is that it's a magical hybrid created by a rogue Telvanni wizard. The coloration of the Tuxedo Vvardvark, according to this theory, was intended to enable it to hide in a flock of chub loons.

1214.name: Karthwolf Shepherd
1214.description: The Reachmen of Western Skyrim use their domesticated ice wolves to protect their clans' livestock. They also keep the herds healthy, as the Karthwolves themselves will cull out the weaklings.

1232.name: Dwarven Theodolite
1232.description: This construct was a sort of automated measuring device designed to explore and survey subterranean areas, according to scholars of the lost Deep Elves—except for Narsis Dren, who insists it was an object of pursuit in Dwemeri team sports.
1232.hint: Acquired by finding its seven parts in Nchuleftingth, and combining them.

1237.name: Bust: Assembly General
1237.description: Bronze bust commemorating an Undaunted victory in the Halls of Fabrication.
1237.hint: Awarded for completing Veteran Halls of Fabrication.

1241.name: Vvardvark
1241.description: The Common, or Demotic Vvardvark has become, in just a few years, an everyday sight on the island of Vvardenfell. But where did they come FROM? Popular opinion points the finger at the wizards of House Telvanni—but they get blamed for everything.

1250.name: Ebon Dwarven Horse
1250.description: Though most ancient Dwemer automata are constructed primarily of the so-called Dwarven Metal, some rare and special animunculus mounts use a preponderance of Ebony. Creations like the Ebon Dwarven Horse are especially durable.

1251.name: Vitrine Dwarven Horse
1251.description: "A horse-shaped Dwarven mount constructed of Ebony, Adamant, Dwarven Metal, and Glass? Sure, why not? The Dwemer could build almost anything, and seemed determined to prove it." —Herebane, Nord "Scholar of the Vanished"

1252.name: Ebon Dwarven Senche
1252.description: Certain rare Dwarven senche vamidiums are constructed with key mechanical components forged, not of the usual Dwarven metal, but of ebony and ebony-steel alloys.

1253.name: Vitrine Dwarven Senche
1253.description: "When considering the Dwarven automaton mounts, the so-called vamidiums, one gets the sense that the Deep Elves were not attempting to replicate nature, but to improve upon it. Case in point: the Vitrine Senche." —Thelwe Ghelein, Scholar of the Dwemer

1254.name: Vitrine Dwarven Wolf
1254.description: Of all known Dwarven mounts, or vamidiums, one of the rarest is the Wolf animunculus with critical components made, not of Dwarven Metal, but of some sort of Dwemeri Glass.

1301.description: Trophy taken from the Earthgore Amalgam in honor of an Undaunted victory in Bloodroot Forge.

1303.name: Nightmare Senche
1303.description: A night-black senche-tiger with burning paws and flames hissing from its face: this is surely the stuff of evil dreams. The origin of this horrific mount is obscure, but some see the hand of Mehrunes Dagon in it.

1330.name: Cinder Wolf
1330.description: This appears to be a reanimated undead corpse of a wolf mount that was burned to death in some horrific event, and has returned hell-bent on vengeance. An intimidating ride, for sure!

1332.name: Karthwolf Charger
1332.description: In the valley of the Karth, the Reach clans have domesticated the fierce ice wolves, which they have bred for size and endurance to serve as mounts. A raiding party of Reach warriors riding Karthwolf Chargers is a fearsome sight indeed.

1335.name: Skeletal Pack Wolf
1335.description: When the Two Moons are full, the undead wolf pack rises from the grave, point their canine craniums at the sky, and try to howl—but the only sound is a dismal rattling in their bony throats.

1336.name: Jackdaw Daedrat
1336.description: The planes of Oblivion are infinite in their variation—and so are their vermin. The Jackdaw Daedrat is a bony Daedric rodent that likes to collect shiny things like your jewelry, and nip and nibble at things it shouldn't, but at least it's cute, right?

1337.name: Skeletal Senche-Leopard
1337.description: Is Necromancy always wrong? Not even death can stop this loyal senche-leopard from stalking to adventure at your side!

1345.name: Haunted House Cat
1345.description: If one lives in a house haunted by spirits of the departed, acquiring a Haunted House Cat to keep the ghosts company will distract them from haunting you. The fact that it can see the spirits of the dead doesn't keep this cat from being sweet and sociable.

1356.name: Shadowghost Horse
1356.description: Shadowghost Horses are never bred, only found, and then only on misty nights when both moons are dark. Then they are summoned from beyond by hooded Shadowghost Wranglers, roped and saddled and broken for riding by ordinary mortals.

1359.name: Witch Knight Charger
1359.description: During their invasion of High Rock, the Reachmen were profoundly impressed by the power and splendor of the Breton mounted knights, and decided to breed their own hardy northern steeds to the same size. They succeeded!

1360.name: Frost Draugr Charger
1360.description: Now seen well outside Skyrim, these skeletal horses once served among Ysgramor's soldiers and were honored after their deaths—or so says one of the epic ballads found in Solitude's Bards College. Dare you ride a steed of such provenance? Of course!

1361.name: Nix-Ox War-Steed
1361.description: It was the warlike Erabenimsun tribe of Ashlanders who first broke the wild Nix-Oxen of Vvardenfell to domestic use, and an ashkhan, the legendary Ashu-Ammu, who first rode one into battle.

1362.name: Plague Husk Senche
1362.description: "Some argue that nothing good came from the Llodos Plague, but I disagree. Ride this noxious necromantic senche, and you'll quickly find all the Peryite followers in a crowd. Perfect if you're hunting one down."—Sondryn Fyr, Assassin

1371.name: Dire Pony
1371.description: When you always wanted a pony as a child and your parents wouldn't let you have one so you grew up bitter and tormented and became a dark cultist but now you can finally afford a pony.

1372.name: Plague Husk Horse
1372.description: A zombie horse is fearsome enough—but a Plague Husk Horse, wreathed in a glowing miasma of toxic infection, is a truly terrifying mount!

1373.name: Shadowghost Senche
1373.description: An oversized breed of black senche-panthers, the Shadowghost Senche is said by the Khajiit to be sacred—or rather unholy—to Namiira the Great Darkness, who sends them as mounts to bear away those who are doomed to die.

1374.name: Shadowghost Pony
1374.description: It's said that to catch a Shadowghost Pony, one should seek out a cemetery on a dark night during Witches Festival and wait quietly near the grave of a child. Bring a carrot or sweet apple.

1376.name: Frost Draugr Senche
1376.description: What were senche-tiger mounts doing in ancient Skyrim, and why were their half-frozen bodies mummified beside the Draugr in certain dark Nord catacombs? And why are they rising now, imbued with animating frost magic? The answers are as yet unknown.

1377.name: Cinder Skeletal Senche
1377.description: "Long-held grudges and rage simmer within this skeletal senche—fitting given its supposed origin as a battle steed for Orcs fighting within the Ashen Forge! This mount's riders gain the utmost respect from Malacath's adherents."—Erisa Moorcroft

1378.name: Skeletal Cat
1378.description: Even dark necromancers have feelings—some of them, anyway—and love their companion pets. Some love them so much they reanimate them after they pass away.

1380.name: Clockwork Skeevaton
1380.description: Originally designed for probing tiny, inaccessible areas of the Clockwork City, the mechanical Skeevaton can be set to recognize and follow an individual mortal, replicating pet behavior on the surface of Nirn.

1381.name: Shadowghost Wolf
1381.description: Unlike nearly all other wolves, the Shadowghost Wolf has no pack and lives a solitary life, haunting lonely moors and wastelands, appearing only at night and rarely then. Some doubt it is a real creature of the mortal plane at all.

1387.name: Shadowghost Pack Wolf
1387.description: Unlike their lone cousins, the great Shadowghost Wolf Mounts, the smaller Shadowghost Pack Wolves hunt on the darkest nights in howling groups. Separated from their packs, they make loyal companions.

1392.name: Flame Atronach Camel
1392.description: When Peregrine Direnni passed her Master Conjurer test by summoning the first-ever Flame Atronach Camel, her mentor Corvus gave her high marks but was heard to comment, "Now you're just showing off."

1393.name: Flame Atronach Guar
1393.description: Flame Atronachs are summoned from the Oblivion plane of Infernace, a realm so hot that molten rock flows across its surface, and its Daedra are creatures of living flame. Summoned to Tamriel, such atronachs can be given almost any shape, even a Guar!

1394.name: Flame Atronach Bear
1394.description: When the Empress Hestra led her legions in harrying the Vampire King Styriche and his Gray Host into western Hammerfell, it's said she did so while riding a great Flame Atronach Bear Mount named Fiery Ursula.

1395.name: Shadowghost Guar
1395.description: Blending in with the shifting gray ash clouds on the slopes of Red Mountain, the Shadowghost Guar are the only known nocturnal breed of the species, and thus are rarely seen, even by the native Dark Elves.

1396.name: Shadowghost Guar
1396.description: Rarely seen outside the ash clouds of Vvardenfell's great volcano, the little Shadowghost pony guar is scary cute.

1409.name: Flame Atronach Horse
1409.description: It was the master summoners of the Direnni who first discovered that a conjurer could impose any desired shape on a Flame Atronach—even that of a horse. Direnni mages mounted on flaming horses first appeared at the Battle of Glenumbria Moors.

1410.name: Flame Atronach Senche
1410.description: For centuries the conjurers' standard spell for summoning Flame Atronachs has been Koron's Peremptory Summons, which is easily modified to change both the duration of the summoned atronach's binding and its form—for example, into that of a senche-tiger.

1411.name: Flame Atronach Wolf
1411.description: "An oversized Flame Atronach Wolf makes for an impressive mount," wrote arch-conjurer Corvus Direnni, "but it's inconvenient to house such a steed in flammable stables. When I'm not riding mine, I temporarily lodge it in a pocket realm Adjacent Place."

1412.name: Flame Atronach Bear Cub
1412.description: Summoned from the Infernace plane of Oblivion, this Flame Atronach variant is given the form of a charming little bear cub. Good for warming hearts and hands alike!

1413.name: Frostbane Sabre Cat
1413.description: Sabre Cats, of course, are inured to the harsh, wintry conditions of Skyrim, and scarcely need warding from the cold; kitting them out as Frostbane mounts is therefore more a question of tradition than of protection.

1414.name: Shadow Atronach Senche
1414.description: Summoned from Oblivion, this shadow atronach was made all the more grand by being compelled to take the form of a senche mount. It's popular amongst those who wish to move quickly and quietly through the more dangerous realms of Tamriel.

1415.name: Flame Atronach Senche-Jaguar
1415.description: The first summoner of this fiery kitten was attempting to compel the Daedra into the form of a full-grown senche-jaguar. Though initially embarrassed by her mistake, she nonetheless grew an attachment to this far more adorable form.

1416.name: Flame Atronach Pack Wolf
1416.description: "Though smaller than its mount counterpart," wrote arch-conjurer Corvus Direnni, "it's necessary to take all precautions when handling the Flame Atronach Pack Wolf. I've found their curiosity insatiable, especially when near flammable objects."

1417.name: Flame Atronach Pocket Horse
1417.description: Due to the unusually tame nature of the Flame Atronach Pocket Horse, it has a long tradition of being the companion of younger members of the Direnni clan. It's a good introduction to Daedric summoning for any budding conjurer.

1418.name: Cold-Flame Atronach Wolf
1418.description: After years of conjuring, Peregine Direnni sought a new Daedra to compel to be her mount. She took an immediate liking to the Cold-Flame Atronach, found in the Daedric realm of Takubar. Summoning it in the form of a wolf just added extra flair.

1427.name: Skyfire Guar
1427.description: This colorful guar was once thought to be poisonous by many, but found to be relatively harmless by an adventuresome rider. Caution! Patience is needed to bring this obstinate mount to heed.

1431.name: Prodigious Brass Mudcrab
1431.description: These perky metal creations are known to pack quite the pinch. Though their rust-resistant coatings do enable them to enter into water, they're far better at sinking than swimming.

1432.name: Helkarn Wolf
1432.description: Hailing from the heart of Elsweyr, these striped mounts are known for their gentle and trusting natures. Once they found them incompetent as watchdogs, the villagers of Helkarn bred them to mountable size.

1437.name: Winter Garland Dapple Gray
1437.description: This festive horse is sure to spread holiday cheer! The proud owner of such a steed can be almost assured that they have the handsomest horse in town.

1440.name: Ebony Brassilisk
1440.description: This experimental variation on the standard Brassilisk has certain key components fabricated from an Ebony alloy for enhanced durability out in the storms of the Radius.

1441.name: Flame Atronach Pony Guar
1441.description: Compelled to take the form of a small guar, this flame atronach makes for a great traveling companion, especially in colder climates. It's best to summon your newfound friend only when outdoors, since its mischievous nature might lead to accidents.

1444.name: Night Frost Atronach Steed
1444.description: This chilling steed was created from a Frost Atronach that was conjured into the shape of a horse. Perfect for an adventurer visiting a warmer climate, this steed can help you stay cool even in extreme temperatures.

1447.name: Spotted Snow Senche-Leopard
1447.description: Even for the elusive senche-leopard, the Spotted Snow is a rare variety. Despite its frosty-looking fur, this adorable companion makes for a great cuddle buddy during long winter nights.

1448.name: White-Gold Imperial Pony
1448.description: The White-Gold Imperial Pony was said to have made its debut as the birthday present for a noble's daughter, though which family claims this prestige is still hotly debated throughout Cyrodiil.

1456.name: Frostbane Guar
1456.description: Since the Guar is native to warmer climates, the existence of the Frostbane Guar in Skyrim, theoretically protected from the cold by its dangling talismans, may be the strongest argument of those who say the Frostbane wards actually work.

1457.name: Frostbane Wolf
1457.description: The Sacred Wolf was one of the most revered Atmoran animal totems, associated by later Nords with the goddess Mara. The great Frostbane Wolf is therefore one of the most iconic mounts of the ancient Nords.

1472.name: Mages Guild Sentry Cat
1472.description: These short-haired, large-eared cats are a common sight in Mages Guildhalls, where it's said their keen senses enable them to detect all manner of intruders, even those that are magically concealed or from realms of Oblivion.

1473.name: Scorpion Fabricant
1473.description: "Since our Incarnatoriums can be modified to produce Fabricants modeled on almost any creature of Tamriel Above, why are Scorpion Fabricants of differing sizes so popular? They're our most-requested fabs!" says Clockwork Apostle Dringest.

1474.name: Lustrous Nix-Ox Fabricant Steed
1474.description: Before Saints Llothis and Olms had to be confined in the Asylum Sanctorium, they used to ride through the Brass Fortress on holy days on these bizarre Fabricant mounts. But the parades are long gone, and the synthetic steeds have been repurposed.

1484.name: White-Gold Imperial Courser
1484.description: Created after years of extensive breeding, the White-Gold Imperial Courser is said to be the most beautiful horse in all of Tamriel. With its almost ethereal beauty, these horses are owned by only the wealthiest riders.

1485.name: Psijic Brassilisk
1485.description: These rare Brassilisks are powered by blue soul gems brought back from the Psijic hideaway of Artaeum at the end of the First Era by Sotha Sil himself.

1486.name: Foxbat Brassilisk
1486.description: These mysterious green-glowing Brassilisks have been showing up in the environment outside the Brass Fortress. Some Clockwork Apostles suspect there's a rogue Incarnatorium assembling them somewhere out in the Radius.

1487.name: Steam-Driven Brassilisk
1487.description: With soul gems in short supply, the Clockwork Apostles invented this experimental Brassilisk powered by steam stored under high pressure.

4659.name: Scintillant Dovah-Fly
4659.description: The Dovah-Fly is a common sight in the oil-slick ravines of the Clockwork City. While its ornate clockworks are a wonder to behold, it's hard to shake the feeling that it's always watching you.
4659.hint: Acquired by traveling to the Brass Fortress in Clockwork City for the first time.

4664.name: Revolving Celestiodrome
4664.description: A gift from the mysterious Sotha Sil himself, this device displays the superb craftsmanship and meticulous detail that are hallmarks of the work of the Clockwork God.
4664.hint: Acquired by completing the quest "The Light of Knowledge," in Clockwork City.

4665.name: Trophy: Saint Olms the Just
4665.description: Trophy taken from Saint Olms the Just in honor of an Undaunted victory in Asylum Sanctorium.

4666.name: Bust: Saint Olms the Just
4666.description: Bronze bust commemorating an Undaunted victory in Asylum Sanctorium.
4666.hint: Awarded for completing Veteran Asylum Sanctorium.

4667.name: Nix-Ox Fabricant Steed
4667.description: Programmed for obedience and fabricated for endurance, these synthetic Nix-Ox Steeds are the perfect mounts for ranging out from the Brass Fortress across the dangerous Radius.

4671.name: Frostbane Bear
4671.description: The Bear was also one of the ancient Atmoran animal tokens, associated later with the Nord god Tsun, so the Frostbane Bear has historically been one of the most prestigious mounts a tradition-loving Nord could ride.

4672.name: Frostbane Camel
4672.description: Perhaps the Atmoran totems and dread-knots sported by the Frostbane Camel actually do help protect it from the bitter cold of Skyrim. Or maybe camels are just too ornery to care.

4673.name: Storage Coffer, Fortified
4673.description:
|cFFFFFF30 Slots|r

This coffer can be placed in multiple homes, and always accesses the same personal storage space. Unlike bank storage, items in this coffer do not appear at crafting stations.
4673.hint: Available from the Level Up Reward System.

4674.hint: Also available for purchase from Rolis Hlaalu for Writ Vouchers or from any Tel Var General Merchant for Tel Var Stones.

4709.name: Fang Lair Courser
4709.description: In Fang Lair, not even ancient warriors' steeds are safe from reanimation by necromancers! Though to be fair, if you're looking for "grimly impressive," this is the mount for you.
4709.hint: Acquired in the Dragon Bones DLC Collector's Bundle.

4710.name: Masqued "Unicorn" Steed
4710.description: Is that the famed and incredibly-rare creature of legend, the true Unicorn from Hircine's Oblivion realm of the Hunting Grounds? …Well, no, it's a horse with a horn attached to its forehead. But the effect—it's just so magical!

4712.name: True Ghost Horse
4712.description: Not a spectre, not a zombie, not a horse of a spooky color—the True Ghost Horse is the actual shade of a deceased mount, returned from beyond the equine grave.

4713.name: Manelord Nightmare Senche
4713.description: King of the Nightmare Pride, this night-black senche-tiger has burning paws and flames hissing from its face; rumor says Mehrunes Dagon is responsible.

4714.name: Frostbane Horse
4714.description: The ancient Nords who came to Skyrim with Ysgramor worshiped animal totems, and adorned their mounts with symbolic hair-knots and hide strips meant to protect their livestock from the frigid climate. These  "Frostbane" talismans are still in use today!

4720.name: Dragonfire Wolf
4720.description: Ancient legends from the time of the Dragon Wars tell of Dragon Knights riding into battle mounted on colossal flaming wolves. Were they wolf mounts mystically imbued with Dragonfire? Flame Atronachs conjured in the form of wolves? No one knows.

4721.name: Galvanic Storm Steed
4721.description: The Galvanic Storm Steed fuses the power of a Storm Atronach from Oblivion with the bloodline of the Yokudan Chargers, the famous war horses of the Redguards, to create an incomparable mount.

4722.name: Snow-Blanket Sorrel Horse
4722.description: This handsome breed of horse is native to the Colovian Highlands of Cyrodiil, and is a common sight from Chorrol to Bruma. The Snow-Blanket Sorrel is known for its intelligence and high spirits.

4723.name: Tattooed Shorn Camel
4723.description: The dervishes of Rihad shave their Hammerfell camels and tattoo them with mystic symbols sacred to the spirits of the deep desert, to placate those wayward spirits in hopes they'll refrain from leading the camels astray among the dunes.

4724.name: Bal Foyen Circus Guar
4724.description: Like other reptilian creatures, Guar can be bred for bright, even gaudy colors. The Argonians of Dhalmora offer this entertaining variant, a popular performer in Tamriel's traveling shows.

4726.name: Small Bone Dragon Construct
4726.description: This construct resembles a great and fearsome Bone Dragon, but it's actually a product of the Necromancer's art, assembled from modern bird and reptile bones and then reanimated.

4727.name: Unholy Glow Bone Dragon
4727.description: This necromantic construct of reanimated bones resembles a gruesome Bone Dragon, one so charged with unholy power that it emits an uncanny blue glow.

4728.name: Madcap Jester Monkey
4728.description: Say, why does this little chum look at you funny? It must be your face! Ook ook! Ah, ha ha ha ha ha ha ha!

4729.name: Karth Winter Hound
4729.description: The Karth Winter Hound is the snow-white breed of the Markarth Bear Dog, snowy year-round for hunting in Skyrim's snow-capped peaks. Some Reach clans reserve the Winter Hounds solely for chieftains.

4731.name: Flameback Boar
4731.description: Like the Purple Daggerback, the breed of Flameback Boars clearly had some kind of brush with the uncanny that imbued them with magical aspects. Regular boars just don't have crimson glowing eyes and flame-colored bristle crests down their backs.

4732.name: Mournhold Packrat
4732.description: Are you the kind of adventurer who simply Must Loot Everything? Being followed around by the Mournhold Packrat, an actual cargo rodent, tells the world that you're an Acquisitionist who's not going to leave behind a single spoon!
4732.hint: |cffffffPurchasing this pet increases your inventory capacity by 5 slots on all characters account wide.|r

4733.name: Wrothgar Buck Goat
4733.description: The Orcs of Wrothgar have a hardy breed of goats well-suited to the area's rugged terrain and changeable climate. Each goatherd particularly prizes his herd's master Buck Goat; these tend to be both intelligent and pugnacious, good animal companions.

4734.name: Big-Eared Ginger Mouser
4734.description: The Ginger Mouser is a favorite barn cat of grain farmers all across central Tamriel, not just because it keeps the storage bins rodent-free, but also for its affectionate personality and goofy good looks.

4735.name: Karth Winter Pup
4735.description: When the Karth Winter Hound has puppies, it even softens the Briarhearts of the Reachmen. Who's a good barbarian pup-pup, then? Is it you? It IS you!

4736.name: Nightmare Senche Cub
4736.description: Despite the fact that this night-black senche-tiger cub has burning paws and flaming eyes, it's so adorable it might be a nightmare you never want to awaken from!

4737.name: Mage's Sentry Kitten
4737.description: When it's a kitten, the Mage's Sentry Cat is so adorable, it's said that some sorcerers enchant them to stay that age always.

4739.name: Helkarn Wolf Pup
4739.description: The pups of the Helkarn Wolves from Elsweyr are almost as sociable with people as dog puppies, so they get a lot of attention when young. This probably contributes to their docility as mounts when full grown.

4740.name: Bristleneck War Boar
4740.description: Originally from Solstheim, this tempestuous boar exists in two modes: hungry and hungrier! Given that it can carry gear, though, providing it with its favorite fungi is a small matter.
4740.hint: |cffffffPurchasing this pet increases your inventory capacity by 5 slots on all characters account wide.|r

4741.name: Magma Scamp
4741.description: Scamps are lesser Daedra used as servants and menials by a number of different Daedric Princes. The Magma Scamps are servants of Mehrunes Dagon, and can be summoned from his Oblivion plane of the Deadlands.

4744.name: Frostbane Pony Guar
4744.description: Though the reptilian Guar are native to the warmer climates south of Skyrim, the compact Pony Guar have long been popular pets among the aristocracy of Riften. Traditional Nords like to dress them in the Frostbane garb used on more local animals.

4745.name: Frostbane Sabre Cat
4745.description: In "The Tail of Ysgramor's Cat," the Harbinger's Sabre Cat hunting companion is described as being festooned with Atmoran Frostbane talismans, and some tradition-loving modern Nords still decorate their Sabre Cats in the same manner.

4746.name: Frostbane Bear
4746.description: Nords who follow the tradition of hanging Frostbane totems and talismans on their beasts to protect them from Skyrim's bitter cold often do it even when the animals are still young, to get them used to the idea.

4747.name: Frostbane Wolf
4747.description: To accustom their Frostbane Wolves to the click-clacking of dangling talismans and totems, the ancient Nords began dressing their companion wolves in Frostbane garb from an early age.

4748.name: Frostbane Pony
4748.description: The hardy ponies of the frozen north look even shaggier when they're decorated with Frostbane hair-knots and ancient Nord totems. Whether the talismans keep the cold away is impossible to tell, but it's certain these ponies never lose their good cheer.

4749.name: Ashen Fang Lair Courser
4749.description: Sometimes, when necromancers reanimate a creature, they overdo it and imbue the undead entity with an excess of dark conjuration. In the case of the Ashen Courser, this residue of mystical power manifests as a cloud of grave dust and ash.

4751.name: Trophy: Scalecaller
4751.description: Trophy taken from the Scalecaller in honor of an Undaunted victory in Scalecaller Peak.

4752.name: Trophy: Thurvokun
4752.description: Trophy taken from Thurvokun in honor of an Undaunted victory in Fang Lair.

4753.name: Bust: Scalecaller
4753.description: Bronze bust commemorating an Undaunted victory in Scalecaller Peak.
4753.hint: Awarded for completing Veteran Scalecaller Peak.

4754.name: Bust: Thurvokun
4754.description: Bronze bust commemorating an Undaunted victory in Fang Lair.
4754.hint: Awarded for completing Veteran Fang Lair.

4796.name: Shadow-Rider Senche
4796.description: Creatures of "Shadow"—are such things possible? Or is the Shadow-Rider Senche merely a black senche-panther mount wrapped in Illusion spells? Somehow, it just seems too uncanny for that mundane explanation.

4996.name: Big-Eared Ginger Kitten
